data.title: Poiema OBX 2026
data.subtitle: August 3rd–7th | Kill Devil Hills, NC
data.location: Kill Devil Hills, Outer Banks, NC
data.excerpt: Step out of the daily churn for rich interactive lectures, unhurried meals, coastal beauty, and deep Christian fellowship at the Outer Banks.

children.text: The purpose of our retreats is to inform, encourage, and inspire Christian young adults regarding who they are in Christ. We see this as a life-awareness that is essential for everyone’s spiritual walk as well as the wellspring of joy and confidence. After all, we are God’s workmanship (poiema) and we want that to set in, be real to us, and when it does: worldview, apologetics, theology, vocation, and, well…all of life is set and in perspective.
Join us at Kill Devil Hills for four days of ocean breezes, sound biblical teaching, volleyball, laughter, and community with believers from across the region.

data.schedule: Morning devotions & coffee; interactive theological lectures with open Q&A; afternoon ocean time, recreation & volleyball; communal home-cooked dinners; evening sunset devotion & hymn singing.
data.lodging_info: Spacious oceanfront beach houses with communal dining areas, shared rooms, pool access, and direct boardwalk access to the Atlantic shore.

data.title: Poiema Spring 2026 Retreat
data.subtitle: Spring Rest & Study in the Highlands
data.excerpt: A weekend mountain gathering focused on biblical discipleship, fellowship around shared tables, and evening devotions.

children.text: Nestled in the highlands of Virginia, our Spring retreat provides young adults a focused weekend away from normal pressures to reflect on Scripture, sing the historic songs of the church, and enjoy the beauty of God’s creation.

data.schedule: Friday evening welcome dinner and campfire singing; Saturday interactive lectures, scenic hiking, and group discussions; Sunday morning worship and closing fellowship.
data.lodging_info: Mountain lodge cabins with rustic warmth, wood-burning fireplaces, and catered family-style meals.

data.title: Poiema International: Gdańsk
data.subtitle: May 29th–June 8th | Poland
data.excerpt: Taking young adults on retreats to other countries to be immersed in the work of Christ in other parts of the world.

children.text: Poiema International takes young adults abroad to be immersed in the church of Jesus Christ beyond our borders. Our trip to Gdańsk, Poland unites American and European believers across the Baltic coast for theological reflection, exploration of historic Reformation heritage, and partnership with local sister congregations.

data.schedule: 10-day immersive study and service tour: exploring historic Reformation sites, visiting local sister congregations, theological lectures, and cultural immersion across northern Poland.
data.lodging_info: Centrally located accommodations in historic Gdańsk with all regional transit and group excursions included.

data.title: Created as His Workmanship: The Meaning of Poiema
data.author: Pastor Laurence Windham
data.excerpt: Why Paul chose the word 'poiema' in Ephesians 2:10, and what it means for our redemption and daily callings as God's poetic masterpieces.

children.text: In Ephesians 2:10, the apostle Paul writes: 'For we are His workmanship (ποίημα, poiema), created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.' We are not haphazard products of fate, nor are we mere cog-like functionaries. The Greek word poiema signifies a crafted work of art, a poem, an intentional masterpiece.

When we gather at Poiema Retreats, our longing is to rediscover what it means to be living expressions of God’s grace in our generation. When believers step away from the relentless churn of cultural performance and rest together in Christ, the beauty of that divine workmanship becomes unmistakably clear.

data.title: Living Together in an Age of Loneliness
data.author: Elder David Cooper
data.excerpt: Christian friendship is not an optional hobby. Biblical communion requires intentional time, shared tables, and deep mutual affection.

children.text: Modern life connects us to thousands through glowing screens, yet leaves us uniquely starved for real communion. Dietrich Bonhoeffer reminded us that Christian brotherhood is not an ideal which we must realize, but a reality created by God in Christ in which we may participate.
This is why the retreat format matters so much. A weekend around a common table, breaking bread and singing psalms without urgency, reminds our souls of what we were built for.

The purpose of our retreats is to inform, encourage, and inspire Christian young adults regarding who they are in Christ. We see this as a life-awareness that is essential for everyone’s spiritual walk as well as the wellspring of joy and confidence. After all, we are God’s workmanship (poiema) and we want that to set in, be real to us, and when it does: worldview, apologetics, theology, vocation, and, well…all of life is set and in perspective.

Poiema was launched out of a passion to see young adults encouraged in their walk with Christ and to see them operating as vital members of their local congregations. Often overlooked, too often not considered as important (until they are married) and sometimes limited in fellowshipping with peers due to the size of their church; Poiema was started to help yours and ours. And it seems to be working.

We appreciate your financial help. We keep the cost of our retreats affordable; the registration fees do not cover all of our costs. We don’t want expense to be the reason that someone doesn’t attend. All registrations and donations are received by Saint Peter Presbyterian Church in Bristol, Virginia and overseen by our diaconate.
Have a question about upcoming retreats, registration, speaking, or scholarship assistance? Contact Laurence Windham at 423-366-2079 or sppcpastor@gmail.com.
